title: Document history
description: One document over time and every version of it: a constitution and its amendments, a gaming compact and its amendments, extensions and replacements, a code or court rules and their revisions, or any other source that changes. Each version cites its own source record, which holds its citation and archived copies. Stored as content/documents/<first letter of id, or _other>/<id>.yaml (decision record 0018).

id.description: Must equal the file name. Name the document, not a version, e.g. ak-chin-indian-community-arizona-gaming-compact or example-nation-constitution.

kind.description: Open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: constitution, law-code, code-title (one title or chapter of a code), ordinance, gaming-compact, gaming-ordinance, secretarial-procedures (Class III procedures under 25 C.F.R. part 291), court-rules, intergovernmental-agreement, statute, regulation, corporate-charter, articles-of-association, model-law, uniform-act, book, report, web-page, other.

title.description: The name the document goes by across its versions, e.g. 'Ak-Chin Indian Community–State of Arizona Gaming Compact'. A version's own title, if different, is in its source record.

nations.description: Tribe profile ids of the nations whose document this is or that are parties to it.

states.description: States or territories that are parties to the document, such as the state party to a compact.

summary.description: Markdown. One or two neutral sentences on what the document is and how its versions relate. The project's own judgments are labeled (project analysis).

versions.description: Every known version, oldest first. A version is any text that took effect, was proposed, or was published as the document at some time: the original, each amendment, a restatement, a replacement, an extension, a new edition. Versions that were found listed but not yet read are still recorded, with verification saying so.

related.description: Other document histories this one depends on or that depend on it, such as the gaming ordinance a compact requires.

document.description: Id of another record in content/documents/.

relation.description: How the other document relates to this one. replaced-by and replaces are for a document that took the place of another under a different name, such as Secretarial Procedures issued where no compact was reached.

found_in.description: Research session ids (file names without .md) that built or updated this history.

version.description: One version. Its citation fields describe the version itself: `source` is the source record of this version's text (with its Indigo Book citation and archived copies), and `verification` says how closely that text was checked. The source record names this version back in its document_version field.

id.description: Unique within the record and stable once published. Suggested form: the year and the event, e.g. 1993-original, 2009-amendment, 2021-restatement.

label.description: How readers know this version, e.g. '2003 compact' or 'Agreement to Amend Compact (2008)'.

event.description: What this version did. original: the first known text. amendment: changes some provisions of an earlier text, which stays in effect as amended. revision: a new text of the whole document adopted by the same process, such as a revised constitution. restatement: a full text that amends and restates an earlier one (an 'amended and restated' compact). replacement: a new instrument that takes the place of an earlier one. extension and renewal: continue an earlier text's term. edition: a new publication or compilation of the same law, such as a recodified code or a court's reissued rules. repeal and expiration: the document, or a version, ends. disapproval: a reviewing authority refused it. withdrawal: a party withdrew it before it took effect.

status.description: Whether this version is in effect as of the record's last check. An earlier text that an amendment changed stays in-effect, as amended; a text that a restatement, replacement or revision took the place of is superseded. unknown: the sources found do not say.

dates.description: Each date the sources give, as a year, year and month, or full date. Record only dates a source states; leave out the rest, and leave out the whole field for a text that gives no date.

signed.description: Executed by the parties or officers.

adopted.description: Adopted or ratified by the enacting body or the voters, such as a council resolution or a secretarial election.

submitted.description: Submitted for a required approval, such as to the Secretary of the Interior.

approved.description: Approved, or deemed approved, by an authority whose approval it needs (see approval).

published.description: Published as required, such as notice of approval in the Federal Register.

listed.description: A date an official list or index gives for the document without saying which event it marks. Used only until a source says what the date is.

ended.description: Stopped being in effect: superseded, expired, repealed or terminated.

approval.description: The action of an authority whose approval the version needs, such as the Secretary of the Interior under 25 U.S.C. § 2710(d)(8) for a compact or under 25 U.S.C. § 5123 for a constitution adopted in a secretarial election.

authority.description: Open vocabulary. Suggested: secretary-of-the-interior, national-indian-gaming-commission, state-legislature, governor, tribal-council, voters.

action.description: deemed-approved: considered approved because the authority did not act in time, as 25 U.S.C. § 2710(d)(8)(C) provides for compacts.

source.description: Source record of the approval or its notice, such as a Federal Register notice.

amends.description: Ids of the versions in this record that this version amends, extends or renews; they stay in effect as changed.

supersedes.description: Ids of the versions in this record that this version takes the place of. Each of them should be superseded once this version is in effect.

capture.description: The project's private copy of this version, kept with the project's working files and never committed or published. Its source record's archives hold the public archived copies.

path.description: Path under the project's working files, e.g. research/captures/gaming/compacts/arizona/<file>.pdf.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the copy, in lowercase hexadecimal.

clauses.description: Key clauses as this version states them. A version that only amends other provisions records here only what it says about a topic itself; whether the topic changed goes in changes.

changes.description: How each tracked topic differs from an earlier version. Every topic recorded in the clauses of this version or of a version it amends or supersedes needs one entry here (scripts/lint_records.py, check clause-change), even if the answer is unchanged or not-compared.

topic.description: Open vocabulary. Suggested: dispute-resolution, judicial-power, peacemaking, sovereign-immunity, renegotiation, term, revenue-sharing, amendment-procedure, election-disputes, removal-and-recall, patron-disputes, membership.

summary.description: One or two neutral sentences on what the clause provides. Not a quotation unless the source's rights allow it.

reviewer.description: Who read the clause, e.g. 'project author' or 'small model, first pass'.

compared_with.description: Id of the earlier version in this record that this one was compared with.

change.description: changed: what the clause provides is different. reworded: the words differ but the process and its effect do not, as when a party's name or a cross-reference is updated. renumbered: moved to a different section without other change. unchanged: compared and found the same, or the version leaves the topic out and says it amends nothing else. not-compared: the comparison has not been made yet.

summary.description: What changed, in neutral words. Required in practice for added, removed, changed and reworded.
